name: Samaritan Pantheon / Sacred Cohort
dom: Samaritan Israelite religion centered on Mount Gerizim
note: Organizing hub for the Samaritan tradition (deity, prophets, priests, eschatology, sacred realm). Modeling device, not an attested 'pantheon' — Samaritanism is strictly monotheistic.

name: Shema (the One God of the Samaritans)
dom: The one God of Israel as worshipped on Mount Gerizim
note: Samaritans confess strict monotheism of the God of Israel; commonly invoke 'Shema' (the Name / the One) and the tetragrammaton-equivalent of Israelite faith. Same God as Israelite Yahweh; distinct cult on Gerizim. Attested in Samaritan liturgy and Pummer.

name: Moses (Samaritan: Moshe, the supreme prophet)
dom: Lawgiver and unique mediator of the Torah
note: In Samaritan theology Moses is the unsurpassable prophet, sole revealer of the complete Torah, sometimes given pre-cosmic dignity in Memar Marqah; no later prophet is canonical. Homonym/reception of the Israelite Moses (ENT_ISR_MOSES).

name: Taheb (the Samaritan Restorer)
note: The Taheb ('the one who returns/restores') is the Samaritan messianic figure, a prophet like Moses (Deut 18:18) who will restore true worship on Gerizim and the hidden cult vessels; attested in Samaritan sources and discussed by Pummer and Anderson-Giles. Functional analogue of the Jewish Messiah.

name: Marqah (Marqe)
note: 4th-c. CE Samaritan theologian, traditional author of the Memar Marqah (Tibat Marqe) and liturgical poems; the great systematizer of Samaritan theology of Moses and the Glory. Historical figure.

name: Baba Rabba
dom: Religious-political reformer of the Samaritan community
note: 4th-c. CE Samaritan reformer who reorganized the community, established sages/hukama and synagogue worship, traditionally associated with a Samaritan revival; historical figure attested in the Samaritan chronicles and Anderson-Giles.

name: Samaritan High Priest (the High-Priestly Line)
dom: Hereditary high priesthood of the Samaritans
note: The hereditary Samaritan high priesthood, claimed from Aaron/Levi via Phinehas (and after that line's end, from the Levitical line of Uzziel); the living head of the community on Gerizim. Continuous office, well attested.

name: Phinehas (Samaritan priestly ancestor)
dom: Eponymous ancestor of the high-priestly line
note: Phinehas son of Eleazar son of Aaron is venerated as the zealous priest and ancestor of the Samaritan high-priestly line (the 'Pinhasite' priesthood). Pentateuchal figure read through Samaritan priestly genealogy.

name: Mount Gerizim (Har Brakha / Argarizim)
dom: The chosen sacred mountain and cult-center
note: Mount Gerizim is the Samaritan 'chosen place' (the tenth commandment in the Samaritan Decalogue), site of the temple/altar, the Passover sacrifice, and the eschatological restoration; the central sacred realm of the religion. Archaeologically and textually attested.

name: The Glory (Kavod / the divine Light)
dom: The manifest divine Glory/Light revealed to Moses
note: Samaritan theology (esp. Memar Marqah) develops the divine Glory/Light (the Kavod) as God's manifestation at Sinai and upon Moses' face; a mediating presence akin to but distinct from the Jewish Shekhinah/Kavod. Attested in Marqah.

name: The Angel of the LORD (Samaritan Malak)
dom: Created angelic mediator of the divine presence
note: Samaritan theology recognizes the Angel/Malak as a created mediator of God's word and presence (e.g., the Angel at the burning bush and Sinai), within a strictly monotheistic framework; discussed in Pummer and Memar Marqah.

name: Samaritan Torah (Samaritan Pentateuch)
note: The Samaritan Pentateuch (Samaritan Hebrew Torah) is the entire Samaritan canon, with distinctive readings (notably the Gerizim commandment); the Abisha Scroll is its most venerated copy. Well attested textual tradition.

name: Samaritan Passover Sacrifice (Pesach on Gerizim)
dom: Annual paschal lamb sacrifice on Mount Gerizim
note: The living Samaritan Passover sacrifice on Mount Gerizim is the most distinctive surviving Israelite blood-sacrifice; publicly attested annual ritual. Modeled only at the level of public observance, not ritual interiors.

name: Joseph (Samaritan ancestor of the Josephite tribes)
dom: Tribal ancestor of Ephraim and Manasseh
note: Samaritans identify principally as descendants of Joseph through Ephraim and Manasseh (the 'B'nei Yosef'); Joseph and Gerizim/Shechem are central to their self-understanding. Reception of the Pentateuchal Joseph (ENT_ISR_JOSEPH).

name: Joshua (Samaritan: builder of the Gerizim altar)
dom: Conqueror who established worship at Gerizim/Shechem
note: In Samaritan tradition (incl. the Samaritan Book of Joshua/Chronicle) Joshua leads Israel into the land and establishes the sanctuary at Gerizim near Shechem, inaugurating the period of Divine Favor (Rahuta). Reception of the Israelite Joshua (ENT_ISR_JOSHUA).

name: Rahuta and Fanuta (Favor and Disfavor)
note: Samaritan periodization of sacred history into Rahuta (the era of divine Favor, from Moses/Joshua) and Fanuta (the era of divine Disfavor/turning-away, beginning with Eli's schism), to be ended by the Taheb. Attested in Samaritan chronicles and Pummer.
